root_cause.text: The bcmgenet_timeout handler erroneously reset all TX queues (via bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all and netif_tx_wake_all_queues) upon a single queue timeout, causing race conditions with other queues that were still actively transmitting.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the per-ring loops with per-queue operations: `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all(dev)` becomes `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim(dev, ring, true)`, and `netif_tx_wake_all_queues(dev)` becomes `netif_tx_wake_queue(txq)`. The commit description explicitly states: "The bcmgenet_timeout handler tries to take down all tx queues when a single queue times out. This is over zealous and causes many race conditions with queues that are still chugging along."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix timeout handler to scope recovery actions to the specific TX queue that timed out, avoiding side effects on other queues.
intent_record.what: Changed bcmgenet_timeout to handle only the specific TX queue that triggered the timeout, replacing loops over all queues with per-queue operations: dump TX queue, reclaim (using bcmgenet_tx_reclaim), re-enable interrupt, update transmission timestamp, and wake queue.
intent_record.how: The timeout handler now only affects the queue indicated by the txqueue parameter, reducing unnecessary work on other queues and preventing potential interference with their normal operation.

grouping_result.intent: Fix timeout handler to scope recovery actions to the specific TX queue that timed out, avoiding side effects on other queues.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by fixing the timeout handler to only reset the specific TX queue that timed out, instead of all queues, thereby preventing race conditions with other active queues.

candidates.rationale: This function reclaims all TX queues regardless of which queue timed out, causing race conditions with other queues still transmitting.
This function wakes all TX queues, potentially starting transmissions on queues that should not be awakened, leading to race conditions with active transmissions.
This line inside a loop over all queues enables interrupts for all TX queues, which may incorrectly re-enable interrupts for queues still actively transmitting, contributing to the race condition.

    - support for RX/TX checksum offload and SG
